own_solution.law: Longitudinal wave speed in a thin rod v_rod = sqrt(E/rho); free-free fundamental (clamped at middle) L = lambda_rod/2 so f = v_rod/(2L); in air lambda_air = v_air/f; dust heaps at nodes spaced lambda_air/2 = L*v_air/v_rod
assumptions: thin rod (diameter << wavelength, no Rayleigh lateral-inertia correction)
light disc does not load the rod
air column driven at rod frequency; node spacing independent of tube terminations

defect_reasons.other: T3295 ('When the clamp is fitted ... for one experiment only') is awkward: it most naturally applies to the present experiment (R), but 'for one experiment only' leaves room to read it as some other experiment.

notes: v_rod = sqrt(7e10/2700) = 5091.75 m/s; f = 5091.75/2.4 = 2121.6 Hz; spacing = 1.2*343/5091.75 = 0.080837 m. With 32 cm added before clamping (clamp then at middle of 1.52 m rod): 1.52*343/5091.75 = 0.102393 m. Cross-section/diameter cancel (area enters both stiffness EA and mass per length rho*A); could also be argued K (thin-rod regime, d << lambda_rod = 2.4 m, holds for 8.21 mm and for 14.3 mm equivalent of 1.6 cm^2). Diameter sentences pair T94AF/T9574 (8.21 mm), area sentences pair T641F/T1BAE (1.6 cm^2): consistent numbers within each pair. T641F attaches the area to the stock, which a rod cut from it shares; either way no effect.
